card.name: Linking words in place descriptions
card.fires_on: Small linking words (in, is, a comma, along, into) right after a river, creek or county name in descriptions of where a place or territory lies. Mostly history and geography text about US regions.

modes.label: In after a river or creek
modes.description: The word 'in' follows a river or creek name and introduces a direction or location.
modes.example: By 1700, the Natchez occupied a territory that covered only an area roughly between Fairchilds Creek and South Fork Coles Creek<< in>> the north to St. Catherine's Creek

modes.label: Comma or verb after a county or area
modes.description: A comma or 'is' follows a county or area name inside a location phrase.
modes.example: About nine miles south of the town of Vienna in eastern Dorchester County<<,>> the landscape transforms from agricultural fields and pine

card.writes: It seems to lower the chance of mountain, hill and beach words coming next, which fits flat river and county settings.
card.plain: It fires on small linking words in phrases saying where a river, county or territory lies.
